results.title: Our style guide for curation of Moments | X Help
results.content:
Users can delete their posts, set their accounts to private or block the relevant @XMoments handle to remove their posts from Moments.

Hashtags

We should not include hashtags in Moment titles, as they’re not clickable for readers.

Words within hashtags may be capped, to improve readability within a description or post (e.g. #StarWarsDay vs #starwarsday).

Health and science studies

In our view, a good health or science Moment:

   Presents the entire story.

   Provides the necessary context to understand the research.

   Doesn’t overstate the study results.

We start by looking at the study itself:

   Where is it published?

   Is it peer-reviewed? (That means other experts in the field have evaluated the methods and results).

   What was the sample size? [...] Right approach: A man armed with knives was shot and killed by police.

It’s OK to use posts including phrases such as “police-involved shooting” if they provide the necessary context.

All usual Curation policies surrounding allegations of wrongdoing apply.

Polling

Moments based on opinion polls must include enough information and context for people to evaluate the importance of the results. At a minimum, we should always cite the source of the poll, when it was fielded and what the sample size was. Titles and descriptions must also avoid exaggerating the meaning of the findings. Remember that polls can be wrong, are only a sample of public opinion, and people can change their minds between responding to one and casting their vote. [...] Skip to main content

## 3) Using hashtags to complain on Twitter

Really? Must you? Inventing your own? Unless you have hundreds of thousands of Twitter followers who are all going to rt you why are you bothering? Who is going to look? Who is going to care? Perhaps find and use a hashtag so your tweets come up as one of many,  but think about it, how often do you look up a hashtag that you don’t know exactly what it is for and join in?!

## 4) Repeatedly tweeting your complaint on Twitter [...] I have been waiting for a refund from Ryanair for a flight they cancelled in March. We were due to fly to Alicante on June 2nd but they cancelled our flight. I have filled in all relevant refund forms and spoken to them on several occasions but all promises are not forthcoming.  
 It is so frustrating they just don’t care.
